newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bonds lack conviction, correction stalls.
newsitem.headline: Australian bonds lack conviction, correction stalls.

text.p: *Australian bond yields closed higher on the day after the market continued to correct the rally seen earlier this week, but overall the move lacked conviction.
*Treasury offering A$200 million 2020 indexed bonds on Thursday.
Australian bond yields closed higher on the day after the market continued to correct the rally seen earlier this week, but overall the move lacked conviction, traders said.
Disappointment that the Reserve Bank has made no announcement on policy since last week's extremely weak labour force report has been putting some pressure on the short end.
However, bill futures are still pointing to lower cash rates with September bill futures at around 94.80 still indicating a cash rate well below current official 5.5 percent interest rates.
Analysts now believe that if the RBA is going to ease again it was more likely to be around the time of the board meeting on July 1 and the Federal Open Market Committee meeting on July 1 and 2.
At the same time, the central bank would get a further update on the retail sector after the back-to-back negatives in the retail trade data in March and April.
May Australian retail trade is due on July 2.

The local market showed a slight widening bias as it awaited direction from local data. Traders termed the move as consolidative given the significant narrowing in yields that has occurred since the last RBA easing on May 23.
